facts.statement: Jinfengopteryx fossils were discovered in the Qiaotou Member of the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China.
facts.quote: It was found in the Qiaotou Member of the Huajiying Formation of Hebei Province, China

facts.statement: The animal likely lived approximately 122 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: and so probably dates to around 122 Ma (122 million years) ago

facts.statement: The species is known from a single nearly complete skeleton, specimen CAGS-IG-04-0801, measuring 55 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Jinfengopteryx is known from one specimen (number CAGS-IG-04-0801), a nearly complete articulated skeleton, which measured 55 cm long

facts.statement: The specimen preserves extensive pennaceous feathers but lacks flight feathers on its hind legs.
facts.quote: It was preserved with extensive impressions of pennaceous feathers, but it lacks flight feathers on its hind legs

facts.statement: Small reddish-yellow oval structures preserved in the fossil may be seeds the dinosaur ate, suggesting an omnivorous diet.
facts.quote: It also preserves several small, oval structures that are reddish-yellow in color, possibly seeds that the dinosaur had eaten before it died

facts.statement: Feather impressions are found around the neck, body, hips, upper hindlimbs, tail, and near the hands.
facts.quote: Jinfengopteryx preserves feather impressions "around the neck, the body, the hips, the upper hindlimbs, the tail, and near the manus"

facts.statement: The dinosaur possessed long, vaned tail feathers that grew progressively longer toward the tip.
facts.quote: Also preserved are long, vaned tail feathers that become increasingly longer distally (away from the body)

facts.statement: The species belongs to the subfamily Jinfengopteryginae.
The animal lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 143 to 128 million years ago, between the Berriasian and Hauterivian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 143 y 128 millones de años, entre el Berriasiense y el Hauteriviense

facts.statement: The animal featured an elongated claw on the second toe of its hind feet.
facts.quote: Este animal presentaba una garra alargada en el segundo dedo de sus patas traseras

facts.statement: The diet is uncertain; despite being a theropod, it may have been a herbivore.
facts.quote: La dieta no está segura. A pesar de ser un terópodo, podría haber sido un herbívoro

facts.statement: The name Jinfengopteryx derives from Jinfeng, the golden phoenix mother of all birds in Chinese mythology, and the Greek word pteryx meaning feather.
facts.quote: Su nombre proviene de Jinfeng, el fénix dorado, madre de todas las aves en la mitología china y del griego πτερυξ, pteryx, que significa 'pluma'

facts.statement: The time range for the genus is recorded as the Barremian stage, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

rejected.statement: A 2020 study indicates Jinfengopteryx had flight capacities similar to other flying non-avian theropods like Microraptor and Rahonavis.
rejected.quote: A 2020 study on paravian flight capacities demonstrates that Jinfengopteryx matches closely with other flying non-avian theropods like Microraptor and Rahonavis
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'other flying non-avian theropods like Microraptor and Rahonavis'

rejected.quote: In 2007, Turner and colleagues did find Jinfengopteryx to be a troodontid, and referred it to that group, noting that it is the first troodontid specimen to preserve evidence of feathers
